newsitem.title: USA: Fairbanks voters approve sale of city utilities.
newsitem.headline: Fairbanks voters approve sale of city utilities.

text.p: Voters in Alaska's second-largest city have approved a ballot resolution to sell their public utilities for $160.3 million, Fairbanks officials said on Wednesday.

In a citywide election held on Tuesday, voters by a 53.5 percent to 44.8 percent margin approved selling the Fairbanks Municipal Utility System to Golden Valley Electric Association, Fairbanks Sewer and Water Inc., Pacific Telecom unit PTI Communications of Alaska Inc and Usibelli Coal Mine Inc. The remainder of the votes cast on that ballot issue were blank, according to results.

In a second ballot issue, Fairbanks voters by a 64.7 percent to 19 percent margin approved setting up a trust fund with the majority of the sale proceeds. The "City of Fairbanks Permanent Fund" would make some of its earnings available for city and capital and operating expenses.

Some of the sale proceeds were to be dedicated to reducing Fairbanks' city debt. In its offer to buy the city's telephone utility, PTI promised to establish a Fairbanks office and to transfer 100 workers from its Anchorage office.
The vote totals did not include absentee and questioned ballots.
